problem.concept: there is currently no general semantic formalism for representing meaning in terms of vectors.

task.concept: natural language semantics in which words, phrases and sentences are all represented as vectors

method.concept: framework for natural language semantics in which words, phrases and sentences are all represented as vectors, based on a theoretical analysis which assumes that meaning is determined by context
corpus model as a mathematical abstraction of a text corpus
interpret the partial ordering of the lattice as describing entailment between meanings

contribution.concept: framework for natural language semantics in which words, phrases and sentences are all represented as vectors
corpus model as a mathematical abstraction of a text corpus

The meaning of a string of words is assumed to be a vector representing the contexts in which it occurs in the corpus model. Based on this assumption, we can show that the vector representations of words can be considered as elements of an algebra over a field.
context-theoretic probability of a string
context-theoretic probability of a string, and, based on this and the lattice structure, a degree of entailment between strings.
framework for natural language semantics: our approach generalises many of these, including vector addition, component-wise multiplication, and the tensor product.

problem.concept: online user comments, which often consist of arguments lacking proper substantiation and reasoning.

task.concept: Identifying Appropriate Support for Propositions in Online User Comments

method.concept: features capturing the verifiability and experientiality

contribution.concept: framework for automatically classifying each proposition
goldstandard dataset of 9,476 sentences and clauses from 1,047 comments submitted to an eRulemaking platform

classifying each proposition: Support Vector Machine (SVM) classifiers trained with n-grams and additional features capturing the verifiability and experientiality exhibit statistically significant improvement over the unigram baseline, achieving a macro-averaged F1 of 68.99%.

task.concept: uncover relationships between content communities post language, such as parts of speech, and user engagement

method.concept: electronic classification and subsequent counting of main parts of speech and other language elements
statistical models are built to examine the relationships between these elements and user engagement, controlling for variables identified in previous research

contribution.concept: The number of adjectives and nouns, adverbs, pronouns, punctuation (exclamation marks, quotation marks and ellipses), question marks, advisory words (should, shall, must and have to) and complexity indicators that appear in content community posts’ titles relate to post popularity (scores: number of favourable minus unfavourable votes) and number of comments. However, these relationships vary according to the category, for example, text-based categories (e.g. Politics and World News) vs image-based ones (e.g. Pictures). Research limitations/implications While the relationships uncovered are appealing, this research is correlational, so causality cannot be implied.
posts from the content community Reddit: language features add explained variance to models of online engagement variables

problem.concept: work on relation extraction has focussed on identifying relationships between entities that occur in the same sentence (intra-sentential relations) rather than between entities in different sentences (inter-sentential relations) despite previous research having shown that intersentential relations commonly occur in information extraction corpora.

task.concept: relation extraction: entities that occur in the same sentence (intra-sentential relations); entities in different sentences (inter-sentential relations)

method.concept: techniques for counter-acting bias in SVM models

contribution.concept: SVM-based approach to relation extraction
the structured features used for intrasentential relation extraction can be easily adapted for the inter-sentential case and provides comparable performance.

method.concept: attributes related to natural language stylometry

contribution.concept: Enron-Spam collection: Classifiers generated by well-known meta-learning algorithms like AdaBoostM1 and Bagging perform equally the best, while a Random Forest (RF) generated classifier performs almost as well.
Enron-Spam collection: The performance of classifiers using Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Naive Bayes (NB) are not satisfactory.
Enron-Spam collection: the performance of Sentinel surpasses that of a number of state-of-the-art personalized filters proposed in previous studies.

problem.concept: Studies on emotion perception often require stimuli with fixed lexical content, but that convey different emotions. These stimuli can also serve as an instrument to understand how emotion modulates speech at the phoneme level, in a manner that controls for coarticulation. Such audiovisual data are not easily available from natural recordings.
record actors reading sentences that portray different emotions, which may not produce natural behaviors.

task.concept: control over lexical content and emotion while also promoting naturalness in the recordings

method.concept: define hypothetical scenarios for each sentence that are carefully designed to elicit a particular emotion
improvise these emotion-specific situations, leading them to utter contextualized, non-read renditions of sentences that have fixed lexical content and convey different emotions

contribution.concept: MSP-IMPROV

alternative approach in which we define hypothetical scenarios for each sentence that are carefully designed to elicit a particular emotion. Two actors improvise these emotion-specific situations, leading them to utter contextualized, non-read renditions of sentences that have fixed lexical content and convey different emotions.

problem.concept: The standard approach to the problem assumes that the set of candidate corrections for a preposition consists of all preposition choices participating in the task.

task.concept: correcting errors in preposition usage made by non-native English speakers

method.concept: exclude candidate prepositions that are not observed as valid corrections in the annotated corpus
take into account the likelihood of each preposition confusion in the non-native text

contribution.concept: methods of restricting candidate sets

correcting errors in preposition usage made by non-native English speakers: restricting candidates to those that are observed in the non-native data improves both the precision and the recall compared to the approach that views all prepositions as possible candidates.
correcting errors in preposition usage made by non-native English speakers: the approach that takes into account the likelihood of each preposition confusion is shown to be the most effective.

problem.concept: hate speech: few scholars have endeavored to systematically define the term
the present scholarship around hate speech rarely extends beyond identification of particular words or phrases that are likely to cause harm targeted toward immutable characteristics.

task.concept: review some of the various attempts to define hate speech, and pull from them a series of traits that can be used to frame hate speech with a higher degree of confidence

method.concept: review some of the various attempts to define hate speech
analyzes historical attempts to define the term in the United States

contribution.concept: eight traits are surfaced that can be used for the development of a confidence scoring system to help ascertain whether a particular expression should be considered one of hate speech or not.

problem.concept: neural approaches for NLG, they are typically developed for particular domains with rich annotated training examples.

task.concept: NLG in a low-resource setting to generate sentences in new scenarios with handful training examples

method.concept: defines a set of meta tasks, and directly incorporates the objective of adapting to new low-resource NLG tasks into the meta-learning optimization process

contribution.concept: Meta-NLG
MultiWoz: Meta-NLG significantly outperforms other training procedures in various low-resource configurations.
MultiWoz: Meta-NLG adapts extremely fast and well to low-resource situations.

problem.concept: Commonly online vandalism has been understood to mean the defacement or destruction of commercial, government or personal websites. This is a rather parochial understanding of the phenomenon which marginalises other more esoteric, but nonetheless prevalent, acts of virtual property destruction.

task.concept: online vandalism: examine the manifestation and regulation of this particular type of online deviance. The study examines ‘deviance’ within a threedimensional online community named Cyberworlds.

problem.concept: few results concern the behavior of l1-penalized estimates for general loss functions.

task.concept: characterizes the asymptotic distribution of penalized parametric M-estimators

necessary and sufficient generalized irrepresentability (GI) conditions for l1-penalized parametric M-estimates to consistently select the components of a model (sparsistency) as well as their sign (sign consistency)
contrast l1-penalized SVM and logistic regression classifiers

contribution.concept: characterizes the asymptotic distribution of penalized parametric M-estimators under mild conditions on the loss and penalty functions in the classical setting (fixed-p-large-n).

necessary and sufficient generalized irrepresentability (GI) conditions for l1-penalized parametric M-estimates to consistently select the components of a model (sparsistency) as well as their sign (sign consistency).
In general, the GI conditions depend on the Hessian of the risk function at the true value of the unknown parameter.
Under Gaussian predictors, we obtain a set of conditions under which the GI conditions can be re-expressed solely in terms of the second moment of the predictors.

We apply our theory to contrast l1-penalized SVM and logistic regression classifiers and find conditions under which they have the same behavior in terms of their model selection consistency (sparsistency and sign consistency).
